3. International Shoe made clear that assessing a defendant’s in-state contacts is not a mechanical act—adding up so many sales or employees in
the forum state—but rather depends on the “nature and quality and the circumstances of their commission.” Based on that standard, how would you
advise a business client whether it is amenable to suit in the following situations:
(a)The client is not incorporated in the forum state, derives 60 percent of its revenue from the sale of widgets in the forum state, the
widgets cause harm in the forum state, and the suit seeks to redress that harm.

(b)The client is not incorporated in the forum state, derives 60 percent of its revenue from the sale of widgets in the forum state, the
widgets cause no harm in the forum state, and the client is sued by a former employee who lives in the forum state for breach of a
contract that is unrelated to the widget.
(c)The client is not incorporated in the forum state, derives one percent of its revenues from the sale of widgets in the forum state, the
widgets cause harm to a tourist who temporarily is in the forum state, and the client is sued by the tourist to redress the injury.
(d)Same facts as (b), but the client sold the widgets knowing that they were toxic and flammable.
